title: Personal Checking: Provisional Credit Sizing and the Number of Submitted Disputes
content:
## Rule

How a Personal Checking provisional credit is sized depends first on how many of the account's electronic-transaction disputes stand in submitted status at the same time.

- **Exactly one submitted dispute.** That dispute is the one under review, and its disputed debit is the ledger entry the dispute names as its disputed transaction. Its provisional credit is sized by the single-dispute determination.
- **Two or more submitted disputes.** The single-dispute determination posts nothing. Each of those disputes, when its credit falls due, is credited at the amount the owner claims on it, never more than the amount of its own disputed debit.

Disputes in any status other than submitted — provisionally credited, resolved either way, or withdrawn — are not counted.

## Counting table

| Disputes in submitted status on the account | How each provisional credit is sized |
|---|---|
| one | single-dispute determination, on that dispute and the debit it names |
| two or more | each at its claimed figure, limited to its own disputed debit |

## Hypothetical cases

- An account has one submitted dispute and one provisionally credited dispute. Only one is submitted, so the single-dispute determination applies to the submitted one.
- An account has two submitted disputes, claiming 50.00 USD on a 50.00 USD debit and 90.00 USD on a 75.00 USD debit. Each is credited on its own when due: 50.00 USD and 75.00 USD respectively.
